purpose: A second, independent pass over the load-bearing external claims in this repository: the competition pages and leaderboard, the official rules document, the reference solution's real contents, and the provenance of the external data.  Every row names the URL, how it was reached, what was observed, and which repository claim it supports.  Nothing here is transcribed from memory, and the two facts that could not be reached from this environment are listed as such.

environment.sandbox_bash_egress: measured again this session: 200 from github.com and pypi.org only; drivendata.org, dropbox.com, sciencebase.gov, pubs.usgs.gov, doi.org, gdr.openei.org and www.nlr.gov are all refused from bash
environment.consequence: official pages can be *read* here but not *downloaded* from bash; the workflows on GitHub runners remain the only route for bulk files

checks.topic: The scoring function, its parameters and the official worked example
checks.observed: TP_w = sum_g max_x p(x)k(d(x,g)); FP_w = sum_{x:p>0} p(x)[1 - max_g k(d(x,g))]; FN_w = sum_g [1 - max_x p(x)k(d(x,g))]; DTI = TP_w/(TP_w + a*FP_w + b*FN_w + eps); k(d) = max(1 - d/R, 0); R = 300 m = 3 px at 100 m; alpha = 0.2, beta = 0.8; official worked example TP_w=3.00, FP_w=1.89, FN_w=2.00 -> 0.60
checks.verdict: CONFIRMED - identical equations and constants; `python src/metrics.py --self-test` check [3] reproduces the published 0.60 from the published components.  Check [4] (reconstruct the example's raster geometrically) still reports FP_w = 2.00 against the published 1.89, because the example PNG is not fetchable from here; the arithmetic check is exact, the raster reconstruction is not.

checks.observed: single layer; CRS EPSG:32611 (UTM 11N); 100 m; same bounds as the training data with null/NaN outside; float32; values 0-1 (probability/confidence)
checks.verdict: CONFIRMED - the writer's contract matches every bullet; the committed submission is float32, one band, 3292x3730, EPSG:32611, NaN outside the data footprint.

checks.topic: Where the training labels come from
checks.observed: "The labels for this challenge come from the USGS quaternary fault maps and from INGENIOUS."
checks.verdict: CONFIRMED - and this is also the reason the SGMC proxy is valid: the proxy sources are *not* QFFD/INGENIOUS, so faults absent from labels.tif are genuinely additional mapped faults.

checks.topic: The SGMC report and the appendix that documents the DESCRIPTION field the proxy selects on
checks.observed: Horton, San Juan & Stoeser, 2017 (ver. 1.1), USGS Data Series 1052, 46 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/ds1052; four state maps are 1:50,000-1:1,000,000; Appendix 5 = 'DESCRIPTION (SGMC_Structure Feature Class) Data Dictionary'; data release https://doi.org/10.5066/F7WH2N65

checks.topic: The INGENIOUS regional compilation (the label source, publicly downloadable)
checks.method: fetch_page (GDR submission, the URL supplied by the user)
checks.observed: DOI 10.15121/1881483, CC-BY-4.0, 116.98 MB across 9 resources + linked datasets; includes 'Quaternary Faults v1.zip' and 'Quaternary Faults v2.zip' ('Attributes conform to USGS Qfault Database schema'), plus conductance, detrended elevation, geodetics, gravity/magnetics, heat flow, seismicity, springs/wells, thermal conductivity, volcanics, study-area boundary
checks.verdict: CONFIRMED, WITH A WARNING FOR THE PROXY DESIGN: the INGENIOUS quaternary fault files are the same lineage as labels.tif, so this source must never be used as an independent fault catalogue - a proxy built from it would be circular.  The SGMC proxy (state geologic maps, largely pre-Quaternary faults, no QFFD/INGENIOUS content) is the independent one.

competition_standing.how_to_read_it: The public leaderboard scores a *public split* of the expert-labelled NEW fault dataset - the same kind of population the prize round scores privately - so it is the only honest signal available. The bar moved in the five days since the previous snapshot (top 0.1972 with 43 ranked, 2026-09-16, now in competition_standing_history): it is a moving target, read it close to the moment you act.
competition_standing.gap: This repository has never been scored by the competition. Producing a submission file is automated (train -> blend -> validate -> committed GeoTIFF), but uploading one needs the entrant's account: the data tab and the submission form both sit behind the login, and the competition rules require the entrant to be a US citizen or permanent resident. Until a human uploads submission.tif (three chances a week), every number in this repository is a local proxy - catalogue DTI, proxy-catalogue DTI, held-out-crop DTI - and none of them is the leaderboard.
